newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1997 export growth seen at 10 pct - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1997 export growth seen at 10 pct - ministry.

text.p: Thailand's Commerce ministry projected in a report released on Friday that the nation's exports in 1997 would grow by 10 percent over 1996.
The Central Bank and Finance ministry have projected zero growth in exports for 1996.

The Commerce ministry added that the country's trade deficit next year would grow by 3.78 percent from 1996 to 595 billion baht. The ministry's data tend to differ slightly from Thai Central Bank data.
The report attributed the expected exports growth, which follows a dismal performance projected for 1996, to anticipated higher growth in the world economy.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) had forecast global economy growth for 1997 to be 4.1 percent against 3.8 percent projected for this year, it added.
According to the IMF, global trade was expected to grow seven percent in 1997 compared with 6.4 percent seen for this year.
